top_fixes.rule: If the customer says the full amount is too much, propose the floor once and say the remainder stays overdue and the account stays in arrears until cleared. Declining the floor is a flat refusal (rule 31). The floor may be named a second time only as attempt 2 (rule 31).
top_fixes.why: After the customer says 'too much' and turns down the floor, rung 0 still becomes the floor. So attempt 1 names the floor a second time, which rule 27/31 forbids. It also delays the flat-refusal path, so the closing outcome/reason and the number of offers are wrong in every 'too much, then decline' case.
top_fixes.fix: check_offer code, rung(): in the `elif rule == 'full_or_floor' and pg(V, pid, 'too_much') == 'yes':` branch, add the condition `and pg(V, pid, 'offered_floor') != 'yes'`. Then the floor replaces the full amount only the first time. Also in check_offer: when offered_floor == 'yes' and the customer declines, set vars['refusal']='flat' and route to the flat-refusal ending (rule 31). The exception is attempt 2: there, allow the floor to be named again only when vars['attempt'] == 2. In negotiate.task_message, add: "You may name the floor amount only once, after the customer says the full amount is too much. Say the remainder stays overdue and the account stays in arrears until cleared. If they decline the floor, treat it as a flat refusal. Do not name the floor again unless this is attempt 2."

top_fixes.rule: The call is to customers whose payment on a single product is between 1 and 45 days overdue: reach the right person, run the security check, explain the overdue amount, agree a payment where possible, and end with the outcome and reason from section 12. Nothing in the brief may be replaced by the assistant's own judgement.
top_fixes.why: prepare code always negotiates prods[0]. It never checks that days_late is between 1 and 45, so a customer with 0 days or more than 45 days late is still negotiated with on green/amber rules, and the call ends with an outcome/reason the brief doesn't allow for that customer.
top_fixes.fix: prepare code: after days_late is computed, add `if days_late < 1 or days_late > 45: vars['out_of_scope']='yes'` (otherwise 'no'). Add a first transition on prepare: `out_of_scope equals 'yes'` -> a fin_out_of_scope code node that sets outcome/reason to the section-12 pair for a case the agent can't handle (for example the no-agreement/callback or transfer reason the brief defines). It should lead to an end terminal with a neutral farewell, so the agent doesn't negotiate. Also make sure only one product is handled (POLICY multi=False is already set).
